author: Drea, Edward J.
title: Japan's Imperial Army: Its Rise and Fall, 1853–1945
notes: The army that source:evans-peattie-1997 is for the navy, and the one that matters most at the start of this arc: how a service came to hold that it could act against the policy of its own government, which is what the Kwantung Army did at Mukden in 1931 and what the pack that opens the arc has to explain. Also the frame for the army's conduct of the island campaigns and its refusal of surrender. Verified against catalogue records only; no ISBN is recorded.
